d: Anantara Hotels & Resorts is a global luxury hotel and resort brand rooted in Thai culture, with an intrinsic sense of authentic hospitality. Inspired by the Sanskrit word meaning ‘without end’, our spirit embodies freedom, movement, and harmony. We believe every journey should leave a lasting impression — for our guests and for our people.

Founded in 2001 in Thailand, we have since expanded across the world, welcoming guests in some of the world’s most captivating locales — from pristine beaches and private islands to ancient sites and vibrant metropolises. If you are driven by a passion for generosity, warmth and heartfelt hospitality, Anantara offers a career without limits.

As an A/C Technician, you will be responsible for the installation, inspection, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of air conditioning, ventilation, and refrigeration systems throughout the hotel. The role ensures that all HVAC equipment operates efficiently and reliably, providing a safe, comfortable, and pleasant environment for guests and colleagues while complying with company policies, manufacturer recommendations, and applicable safety standards.
Install, inspect, service, maintain, and repair air conditioning and refrigeration systems throughout the hotel.
Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on split AC units, package units, VRF/VRV systems, fan coil units, air handling units, exhaust fans, ventilation systems, and other HVAC equipment.
Diagnose faults and carry out necessary repairs to ensure minimal downtime and maximum equipment reliability.
Respond promptly to guest and hotel department maintenance requests, as well as emergency HVAC breakdowns.
Carry out regular inspections of HVAC systems in guest rooms, public areas, back-of-house areas, offices, restaurants, kitchens, and other hotel facilities.
Clean and maintain indoor and outdoor AC units, filters, evaporator and condenser coils, drain lines, and ventilation systems.
Check refrigerant levels, identify refrigerant leaks, and carry out refrigerant charging and recovery in accordance with environmental regulations.
Monitor the performance and efficiency of HVAC equipment and report any abnormalities or potential equipment failures to the Engineering Supervisor.
Maintain accurate records of inspections, preventive maintenance activities, repairs, equipment breakdowns, and replacement of parts.
Coordinate with the Engineering Storekeeper and Engineering team to ensure the availability of required spare parts, tools, and materials.
Identify equipment requiring major repair, replacement, or specialist attention and report recommendations to the Engineering Supervisor.
Ensure all maintenance work is carried out in accordance with local regulations, manufacturer recommendations, and company health, safety, and environmental standards.
Practice proper handling, storage, recovery, and disposal of refrigerants and other HVAC-related materials to minimize environmental impact.
Support other Engineering and maintenance activities within the hotel as assigned.
Maintain a clean, organized, and safe working environment at all times.
Ensure guest comfort and satisfaction by completing maintenance requests efficiently and minimizing disruption to hotel operations.
Actively participate in the hotel's energy conservation and sustainability initiatives.
Suggest cost-saving and energy-efficient solutions to improve the hotel's HVAC operations.
q: Certificate or Diploma from a recognized technical or vocational institute in Air Conditioning, Refrigeration, HVAC, or a related field.
Minimum of one (1) year of relevant experience in HVAC maintenance, preferably within a hotel, resort, commercial building, or facility management environment.
Sound knowledge of air conditioning, refrigeration, ventilation, and HVAC systems.
Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, electrical schematics, and equipment manuals.
Experience with VRF/VRV systems, AHUs, FCUs, and other commercial HVAC systems is an advantage.
Basic knowledge of electrical and mechanical systems related to HVAC equipment.
Familiarity with occupational health, safety, and environmental regulations.
Knowledge of refrigerant handling and environmental requirements.
Ability to work independently, prioritize tasks, and respond effectively to maintenance emergencies.
Good communication, interpersonal, and teamwork skills.
Customer-focused attitude with the ability to respond professionally to guest requests and concerns.
Willingness to work shifts, weekends, and public holidays according to hotel operational requirements.

d: Right now, thousands of people in the UAE book a cleaner through Justlife and expect them to show up on time, do excellent work, and leave their home better than they found it. That promise only holds if the cleaners are there, trained, motivated, and routed efficiently — which means someone has to own the daily operating reality of that supply chain: keeping cleaners deployed, partners accountable, costs disciplined, and quality high.

This is an operations role, not a strategy role. Youll run the DTC home cleaning business end-to-end — 300+ cleaners across multiple partner companies, a small on-ground team of account executives and roster agents, and measurable improvement in on-time performance, completion rates, and contribution margin within your first six months. Every day youll make decisions that move the numbers: which partner hires next, how to incentivise productivity, where fuel and routing waste money, whether were hitting our supply plan. This is what it means to own a real business line.
Youll love this role if you...
You think in unit economics and get frustrated when a cost lever stays hidden in a spreadsheet instead of being fixed
Youve run a large field or blue-collar workforce (directly or through partners) and know exactly how to hold external teams accountable without being their boss
Youre energised by problems you can see and touch — youd rather spend an hour in a van or at a partner accommodation than sit in a meeting
You build teams that work without you, and you actively coach people into bigger roles
You obsess over data quality because you know bad reports kill decisions, and youll learn SQL or Power BI yourself rather than wait for someone to build your dashboard

Drive sustained improvement in on-time %, completion rate %, promise-kept %, and absent rate % by building daily operating discipline — reviewing metrics with the team each morning, identifying blockers, and acting on them before they compound into service failures.

Lead and develop the on-ground operations team (2 account executives and 4 remote roster agents): set clear priorities, review performance daily, coach individuals toward higher capability, and manage accountability.

Own supply planning and growth: forecast cleaner headcount needed against demand by city and partner, manage onboarding pace and allocation across partner companies, and reduce time-to-deployment so new hires contribute faster.

Manage partner companies as senior counterparts: run monthly business reviews, hold them to service-level agreements and commercial terms, reconcile statements of account with finance monthly, and escalate issues before they become crises.

Design and drive cost and process projects that improve contribution margin — incentive structure redesigns, fuel and fleet controls, van routing optimisation, cleaner orientation and training — taking each from idea to measurable result.

Build and maintain reporting that surfaces whats driving performance: which partners are slipping, where attrition is highest, which cost levers moved margin, whats blocking supply. Act on what it shows.
Spend meaningful time in the field — in vans, accommodations, and partner sites — so you understand problems first-hand and your team sees you do the same.
What tells us youre the one

Youve measurably improved operational metrics across a large field workforce — tell us a specific program you ran (incentive redesign, routing optimisation, vendor onboarding, training rollout, etc.) and the metric that moved as a result: completion rate up X%, on-time performance improved Y%, attrition fell Z%, or margin lifted by N%.

You can spot cause and effect: when a metric moves, you know whether its partner execution, process design, incentive misalignment, or something else — and you know how to test your hypothesis before rolling out a fix.

Youve managed blue-collar, field-based, or logistics workforces (home services, facilities management, staffing, last-mile delivery, quick commerce) — or run marketplace operations where supply quality depends on external partners. Results matter far more than years, but 5–7 years of this kind of work is the sweet spot.
Youre fluent in data: you can build operating reports independently, interrogate a spreadsheet without help, and use SQL, Power BI, or AI tools to automate manual reporting so you have time to think.

You speak fluent English, written and spoken. Bonus: you speak languages common to the workforce in the UAE (Tagalog, Urdu, Arabic), or you have prior experience operating in the UAE market in home services, logistics, or staffing.

Scale and impact: Youll run a real, revenue-generating business line serving thousands of customers across the UAE, managing hundreds of cleaners and multiple partner companies, with direct line of sight from your decisions to customer satisfaction and margin.
Clear growth path: this role is a launchpad into broader category leadership, multi-city operations, or general management as we scale across the GCC.
Close partnership with leadership: youll work alongside the Business Development lead and the founding team, with real influence on strategy and resource decisions.
A fair, performance-driven culture: youll be measured on the metrics you own, recognised through our JustHeroes program, and rewarded for results — not politics.
Startup benefits: a birthday day off (JustHoliday), free Justlife service credits, referral bonuses, and regular team experiences.
Join the tribe and lets become #everydaybetter, together.
